## Colab keys

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}} | Run the cell and move to the next one |
| {{< kbd Cmd-Enter >}} (Mac), {{< kbd Ctrl-Enter >}} (Windows) | Run the cell and stay on it |
| **+ Code** | Add a new code cell |
| `len?` | Show help for `len`. Works for any name. |
| **Runtime → Run before** | Run every cell above the current one, after a fresh start |

Only the last line of a cell shows its value. Use `print()` to show more.

## Variables and types

| Code | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `age = 34` | Store a value. One `=` assigns. |
| `age == 34` | Compare two values. Two `==` ask a question and give `True` or `False`. |
| `type(age)` | Show the data type: `int`, `float`, `str`, `bool`, `list`, `dict` |
| `f"I am {age}"` | Put a value inside text (an f-string) |

Names use letters, digits (0-9) and `_`, and can't start with a digit.

## Strings and indexing

Counting starts at 0.

| Code | Result with `word = "python"` |
| --- | --- |
| `word[0]` | `'p'` |
| `word[-1]` | `'n'` |
| `word[0:3]` | `'pyt'` (the end index is left out) |
| `len(word)` | `6` |

## Lists

| Code | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `toys = ["feather", "string"]` | Make a list |
| `toys[0]` | Get an item by position |
| `toys[0] = "laser"` | Replace an item |
| `toys[0:2]` | Slice: items 0 and 1 |
| `toys.append("catnip")` | Add to the end. Changes the list itself. |

## Dictionaries

| Code | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `birthdays = {"Spot": "May 1"}` | Make a dictionary of key: value pairs |
| `birthdays["Spot"]` | Get a value by key |
| `birthdays["Sparky"] = "May 10"` | Add or change a pair |

`[]` on a list takes a position. `[]` on a dictionary takes a key.

## Operators

| Kind | Operators |
| --- | --- |
| Arithmetic | `+` `-` `*` `/` (always a float) `//` (floor division) `**` (power) `%` (remainder) |
| Comparison | `==` `!=` `<` `>` `<=` `>=` |
| Logical | `and` `or` `not` |

## if, for and def

::: {.panel-tabset}
### if

```python
if score >= 90:
    print("A")
elif score >= 80:
    print("B")
else:
    print("Keep going")
```

### for

```python
for i in range(5):
    print(i)

for name in ["Bob", "Bill"]:
    print(name, len(name))
```

### def

```python
def add_nums(a, b):
    return a + b

total = add_nums(2, 3)
```
:::

The colon and the indented lines belong to each other. `print` shows a value; `return` hands it back.

## Methods

Dot notation: `object.method(argument)`.

| Kind | Example | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| String method | `word.upper()` | Returns a **new** value. `word` is unchanged. |
| List method | `toys.append("catnip")` | Changes the list itself. Run it twice and you get two. |

## Common errors

| Error | Usually means | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NameError` | A name doesn't exist yet | Check the spelling, and run the cell that creates it |
| `SyntaxError` | Python can't read the line | Look for a missing quote, bracket or colon |
| `IndentationError` | The indented lines don't line up | Use the same number of spaces in the block |
| `TypeError` | A value is the wrong type for the operation | Check with `type()`, such as `"5" + 5` |
| `IndexError` | The position doesn't exist | Remember the last index is `len(x) - 1` |
| `KeyError` | The key isn't in the dictionary | Check the spelling and capitalization |

Read the last line of the message first: it names the error. The lines above it point to where it happened.

## uv commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `uv --version` | Check uv is installed |
| `uv init --python {{< var python >}} --vcs none dss-python` | Make a project folder |
| `uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab` | Start JupyterLab, installing it on the first run |
| `uv add matplotlib` | Add a package to the project |
